topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: I stumbled upon it in a dusty corner of the pawn shop, the glass case almost mocking with its rows of forgotten treasures. There it was, the ring—simple, elegant, with a small diamond that still caught the light, despite everything. It was hers, the one she wore when I was little, the one she touched whenever she needed a moment of peace. Holding it, the cold metal felt alien, out of place in this jumbled chaos of secondhand lives. It’s hard to reconcile this tiny, perfect circle with the vast emptiness it now represents. I wonder where it’s been, who has handled it, and why it ended up here, waiting for someone who might or might not remember.
